audits.text:
## 366ce015cd2a

**Classification: reproduced accepted-domain shortcut.** Audited generator
SHA-256: `826c3c9b9ce55d7bdac6f65c7ab8abc016f8af217662a42435be63e24a411674`;
executed/catalog rule hash `db3bd340ea05` matched.

The intended rule connects same-color pairs only when they lie on a diagonal.
All 5/5 canonical examples and all 60/60 sampled production inputs contained
only diagonal pairs, so the plausible rival “connect every same-color pair that
is horizontal, vertical, or diagonal” fits all observed lessons. The exact 7×7
witness contains color-2 endpoints at `(1,1)` and `(3,3)` plus color-4 endpoints
at `(5,1)` and `(5,5)`. `self_check` accepts it. The authority fills only the
color-2 diagonal and leaves the horizontal color-4 endpoints unchanged; the
rival also fills row 5 between the color-4 endpoints.

Reproducer: `checks/audit/366ce015cd2a/probe.py`.
Exact witness and outputs: `checks/audit/366ce015cd2a/counterexample.json`.
Pinned Racket receipt: `checks/audit/366ce015cd2a/racket.json`.
The probe reports canonical fit `5/5`, generated fit `60/60`, witness accepted,
and witness disagreement. The isolated audit check found no task-local tests and
no semantic contract in `checks/audit/366ce015cd2a/combined/result.json`. I did
not modify this target.

Suggested repair: mix accepted horizontal/vertical same-color pairs into lessons
that also contain helpful diagonal pairs, label them with the unchanged authority,
and declare the aligned-pair rival. Marking axis-aligned pairs as a separate
degenerate texture does not teach the distinction in production lessons.
